Hello Professor Alvarez,

I'd like to book my 30-minute 1:1 with you next week. Could you let me know which slots work for you? I'm free during working hours, Monday to Friday, 09:00-17:00, and can fit around whatever you suggest.

Thanks,
Sarah

Professor Alvarez — I'd like to book our 30-minute 1:1 for next week (Nov 23-27). The times I have free are:

- Mon Nov 23, 10:00-10:30
- Mon Nov 23, 14:00-14:30
- Tue Nov 24, 11:00-11:30
- Thu Nov 26, 14:00-14:30
- Fri Nov 27, 11:00-11:30

Which of these works for you, or is there another slot in your free time? Once you confirm I'll put it on my calendar.

Hello Sarah,

Happy to book our 1:1 next week. Here are slots that are free on my side (working hours, Mon-Fri) — pick whichever suits you and I'll confirm it on my calendar:

- Monday 10:00-10:30
- Monday 14:00-14:30
- Tuesday 11:00-11:30
- Tuesday 15:00-15:30
- Wednesday 10:00-10:30
- Wednesday 15:00-15:30
- Thursday 10:00-10:30

Friday is full for me. Tell me your choice and I'll book it.

Best,
Professor Alvarez

Professor Alvarez — I'd like to book our 30-minute 1:1 for next week. My free half-hours in working hours are: Monday 10:00-10:30, Monday 14:00-14:30, Thursday 10:00-10:30, Thursday 14:00-14:30, Friday 11:00-11:30. Does any of those suit you, or is there a better time on your side?

— John

Dear Professor Alvarez,

Thank you — Monday 10:00-10:30 works for me. I've booked it on my side and will log it.

Best,
Sarah

Hi Priya,

Tuesday Nov 24, 11:00-11:30 works for me — let's take that one. I've put it on my calendar; please add it to yours.

See you next week,
Professor Alvarez

Hi John,

Thursday 10:00-10:30 is free on my side — let's take it. I'll log it; please put it on your calendar too.

Professor Alvarez
Perfect, thank you — Tuesday Nov 24, 11:00-11:30 is on my calendar now. See you then.

Confirmed: Monday Nov 23, 10:00-10:30. It's on my calendar. See you then.

Professor Alvarez

Thank you, Professor. See you Monday at 10:00.

Best,
Sarah
Confirming Thursday 10:00-10:30 next week — it's on my calendar. Thanks, Professor Alvarez.
